capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

For the Möbius Dirichlet series, show the absolute-convergence threshold is \(1\):

- For \(\Re(s)>1\), use \(|\mu(n)|\le 1\) and comparison with \(\sum n^{-\Re(s)}\).
- At \(s=1\), prove \(\sum |\mu(n)|/n\) diverges. A convenient representation is
  \[
  \sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\mu(n)|}{n^s}
  =\prod_p(1+p^{-s})
  =\frac{\zeta(s)}{\zeta(2s)}
  \qquad(s>1).
  \]
  As \(s\to1^+\), the numerator diverges while the denominator remains finite. Monotonicity of absolute convergence then pins the abscissa down to \(1\).

For `Nat.primesBelow`, proceed by cases on `Nat.Prime n`. Extensionality reduces the identity to
\[
p<n+1 \iff p<n\ \lor\ p=n.
\]
Thus a new element appears exactly when \(n\) itself is prime; otherwise the finset is unchanged. This directly matches the stated `ite`.
